articles.title: Ferguson? Guardiola? Mourinho? Ranking the best managers in Premier League history
articles.summary: Thirteen managers have won the Premier League title, but which of them will make it into our top 10 covering the competition's history?
articles.body:
When it comes to ranking managers, titles are a good place to start.

Only four bosses have won more than one since the Premier League era began in 1992. So if you do some quick maths, you'll probably not be surprised by the names that top this list.

But there is a debate to be had around where they should rank, and who else makes it into the top 10. So let's have it.

You can rank your greatest managers of the Premier League era below too.

Longevity deserves a mention here. Take David Moyes, for example, racking up 755 games in Premier League dugouts - only Arsene Wenger (828) and Sir Alex Ferguson (810) have more.

Naturally, Moyes has the third-most wins in Premier League history too, although his 291 across spells with Everton, Manchester United, Sunderland and West Ham fall some way short of Wenger's 476 at Arsenal and Ferguson's 528 at United.

Pep Guardiola is also on Scotsman Moyes' shoulder despite managing barely half as many games.

Harry Redknapp has the fourth-most games under his belt (641), fifth-most wins (236) and also completes the top five for goals scored (818).

We should talk about win percentage too, and the former Tottenham manager who really deserves a shout here is Mauricio Pochettino, who guided Spurs to their best-ever Premier League finish of second in 2016-17 and also coached Southampton and Chelsea.

The Argentine is the only manager - of those who have coached more than 100 games - to have not lifted the title yet still won more than half his games throughout his Premier League career.

But really, to make this list, you have to have won a Premier League title. In total, 13 managers have done so. Meaning three are getting left at the door.

Arne Slot of Liverpool is the first to be cut. The others are a hard choice.

Manuel Pellegrini's Manchester City record was impressive before the Chilean made way for Guardiola. During those three years, plus 17 months at West Ham, his average of 1.92 goals per game ranks fifth among all managers with a century of matches.

But he spent big at the Hammers only to then endure a desperate run of form - so the man known as the Engineer, the only manager from outside Europe to win the title, misses out.

As does Antonio Conte, who had boom and bust spells at Chelsea and Spurs.

Instead, the pair are pipped by the only boss to win the title in all of Europe's top five leagues.

10. Carlo Ancelotti. Title winner 2009-10

AC Milan, Bayern Munich, Paris St-Germain, Real Madrid and, of course, Chelsea.

King Carlo has steered them all to domestic glory, not to mention his Champions League record of five successes. Yet his initial tenure in the English top flight was fleeting.

The Italian blitzed his way to the Premier League crown at the first time of asking at Stamford Bridge. But, after snapping up Fernando Torres for a then-British record fee from Liverpool the following January, Ancelotti was swiftly shown the door after Chelsea finished as runners-up in his second season.

A surprising return to England came via the Everton dugout, where Ancelotti delivered successive mid-table finishes before Real Madrid came calling.

Earlier this year, Mikel Arteta became the 13th manager to win the Premier League but the first Arsenal boss to do so since Arsene Wenger in 2004.

The Spaniard also snapped an eight-year run of either Manchester City or Liverpool winning the trophy.

Bursting clear of his rivals like they were a technical area, Arteta shrugged off questions over his team's sometimes robust style as well as those who suggested the Gunners were destined to always be runners-up.

As the only current Premier League boss to have won the title, and with Arsenal adding to an already stacked squad this summer, you wouldn't bet against the former playmaker creeping further up this list in future.

8. Roberto Mancini. Title winner 2011-12

Premier League titles don't come more dramatic than two goals in added time - including a 94th-minute winner - on the final day of the season, especially to clinch a first top-flight crown in more than 40 years while denying your arch-rivals.

Roberto Mancini got Manchester City's lavish new era rolling by winning the FA Cup in his first full season, having replaced Mark Hughes in December 2009, and followed up with the title before he was sacked the following summer.

The Italian, though, stacks up well, boasting the fourth-best points-per-game tally for any boss to have managed at least 100 Premier League games - coming in just above Conte and Jose Mourinho - and the fifth-best win percentage.

Meanwhile, his City stars make the top five for goals per game and boast the best record for fewest goals conceded, a miserly 0.83 per game.

Kenny Dalglish's greatest success as a boss came at Liverpool before the Premier League era began, winning three titles in four seasons, initially as a player-manager, before he departed in February 1991 after almost 15 years with the club.

He wound up at second-tier Blackburn Rovers eight months later and immediately steered them into the Premier League via the play-offs.

Bankrolled by local businessman Jack Walker, Rovers snapped up Alan Shearer from Southampton for a British record fee of £3.6m and then finished fourth and second before overcoming Manchester United to win the title in 1995.

That made Dalglish only the fourth manager to win the English top flight with two different clubs.

Dalglish was unable to repeat the trick at Newcastle, although they finished runners-up in both the league and FA Cup during his tenure, while his return to Liverpool ended in 2012 after League Cup success but an eighth-placed finish.

6. Claudio Ranieri. Title winner 2015-16

Dilly ding, dilly dong. Ranieri rides into the top six on pure vibes. The man behind the 5,000-1 miracle. The one who turned a cast of footballing misfits into an all-conquering force. The father of Leicester City's Premier League triumph.

That is worth his entry alone. Yet, in what seems another lifetime, the Tinkerman almost got his hands on a winner's medal more than a decade earlier.

Buoyed by the first wave of Roman Abramovich spending, Ranieri steered Chelsea to second in 2004, only behind Arsenal's Invincibles.

Chelsea probably should have won the Champions League too, losing in the semi-finals to Monaco, but that became a defining moment for the man who would replace him.

Jurgen Klopp is in some ways the Andy Murray of the Premier League. All action, high-octane performances, adored by his fans yet prickly under pressure. He enjoyed incredible success but would probably have dominated more were it not for a generational opponent.

In this rather stretched analogy, Manchester City are Klopp's Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. If it had not been for his Catalan counterpart down the M62, Klopp's rock 'n' roll Reds would have been the undoubted top dogs under the German.

Instead, they racked up more than 90 points on three occasions and 'only' clinched one title in 2019-20 - it was, however, Liverpool's first in 30 years and their first of the Premier League era.

4. Jose Mourinho. Title winner 2004-05, 05-06 & 14-15

Lungs still pumping from that touchline sprint at Old Trafford, Jose Mourinho landed at Chelsea days after guiding Porto to a remarkable Champions League triumph and declared himself a 'Special One'.

Taking the baton from Ranieri and armed with a host of new signings, the Portuguese enigma stormed the title in his first season - Chelsea winning the league by 12 points, conceding only 15 goals and ruffling the raincoats of Wenger and Ferguson.

Mourinho backed it up in his second season before relationships began to fray and the most successful boss in the club's history left in September 2007. Mourinho, though, had transformed the Blues into a formidable force.

He returned six years later, after titles in Milan and Madrid, and clinched his third Premier League crown in his second season, only to be gone by Christmas of the following campaign.

Box-office spells followed at Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur, but they came nowhere near the success of his time in south-west London.

3. Arsene Wenger. Title winner 1997-98, 2001-02 & 03-04

It's fine margins between Wenger and Mourinho, as both their arrivals brought the dawn of new eras in the Premier League.

Indeed, Mourinho once said Wenger is a "specialist in failure", but in this list the Frenchman just pips his rival thanks to engineering the only 'Invincibles' season in Premier League history.

Wenger, joining from Japanese outfit Nagoya Grampus Eight, was deemed a curious choice at first but professionalised Arsenal and led them to league titles in 1998, 2002 and - the piece de resistance - that unbeaten season of 2003-04.

That he was unable to win another title in the 14 years that followed perhaps tarnishes Wenger's legacy slightly, but the Arsenal team he built during his first decade was one of the best the Premier League ever witnessed.

2. Pep Guardiola. Title winner 2017-18, 18-19, 20-21, 21-22, 22-23 & 23-24

Talking of managers who changed the face of English football, no-one has moved the game right from the elite level through to grassroots as much as Pep Guardiola.

Blame the Catalan for Sunday League goalkeepers playing out from the back.

And to think there were question marks over whether Guardiola's style - honed at Barcelona - would work in the more robust English game.

Guardiola was, of course, lavishly backed in the transfer market, but his Manchester City side won titles at a prolific rate.

City became the first English men's side to win four in a row - they landed six Premier League titles in total during Pep's decade in charge, as well as notching a century of points in 2018.

1. Sir Alex Ferguson. Title winner 1992-93, 93-94, 95-96, 96-97, 98-99, 99-2000, 2000-01, 02-03, 06-07, 07-08, 08-09, 10-11, 12-13

The first two decades of the Premier League were dominated by one man.

Sir Alex Ferguson won 13 titles and was able to continuously rebuild his side in order to keep Manchester United at the top of English football - from Eric Cantona to the '99 Treble winners, and later that front three of Cristiano Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney and Carlos Tevez.

Even after Ronaldo left for Real Madrid in 2009, and Tevez defected to the other side of Manchester, Ferguson continued winning titles until he retired in 2013.

His record title haul is more than double any manager from any era of men's English top-flight football, not just the Premier League - Guardiola, Liverpool's Bob Paisley and George Ramsay for Aston Villa are next on the list on six.

It makes Fergie the undoubted number one.

articles.title: Aston Villa: Unai Emery's problems mounting ahead of Arsenal test after threadbare squad falls apart against Brighton
articles.summary: Sky Sports analyses the problems mounting for Unai Emery at Aston Villa following their dismal defeat to Brighton in their season opener; Villa lost 4-0 at the Amex Stadium and Joao Gomes was sent off; Emery's side host Arsenal next, live on Monday Night Football
articles.body:
The Villa boss has been forced to watch on as his Europa League-winning squad has been decimated during the summer transfer window.

Four of the starting line-up from that May final have departed, leaving gaping holes across the pitch, and the situation could worsen before they host Arsenal at Villa Park, live on Monday Night Football .

The seismic changes caused a storm that even the experienced Emery could not weather on the opening weekend.

Villa became just the second team in Premier League history to concede four goals, receive a red card and score an own goal in the first half - after Southampton against Manchester United in 2020/21. Starts to the season do not get much worse.

Emery has navigated slow starts before: Villa did not score a league goal until September 21 last season only to recover and secure Champions League football, but this feels like his biggest challenge yet.

The situation appears bleak but there is no time for self-pity - changes, adjustments and reinforcements are desperately needed.

From bad to worse? More exits on the horizon

Youri Tielemans , Lucas Digne , Morgan Rogers and Ezri Konsa are gone. Ollie Watkins is another big name and cornerstone of the squad approaching an exit amid interest from Al Hilal.

"Ask him. I can only answer it by silence," was the response from Emery when asked why Watkins did not make the trip to the south coast for the defeat at Brighton, as his side unravelled to an embarrassing defeat without a recognised striker named in the squad.

Emiliano Martinez , a stalwart in goal, was also absent and is pursuing an exit after a move to Juventus fell through. His replacement, Zion Suzuki , watched on from the bench as his new side failed to land a blow in the one-sided brawl at the Amex.

Villa's squad retention is the lowest in the Premier League at 65.6 per cent, followed closely by Tottenham at 67.1 per cent.

However, changes at Spurs were needed given back-to-back 17th-placed finishes. Villa's squad has been pulled apart from a point of success.

Joao Gomes , another new recruit and a man Villa were relying on to fill one of the many chasms, was sent off on his league debut at Brighton to add salt to the wound of the dismal defeat.

Record signing Johan Manzambi is yet to make an appearance due to injury and will not be available to face Arsenal, joining Amadou Onana on the sidelines following his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury at the World Cup.

Alejandro Garnacho and Matteo Ruggeri both came off the bench to make their debuts at Brighton, their introductions providing fresh legs more than anything as Emery sought to limit the damage.

Key players have left and their replacements are either unavailable or being kept at arm's length from the upheaval to slowly embed into the team. So, where do Villa turn now?

Toothless - Villa need an option up front

One position that needs addressing sooner rather than later is up front.

Watkins' future at Villa Park is seemingly approaching a bitter and sudden end. The cryptic interview from Emery when quizzed on his absence points to irreparable damage.

Villa turned to Emi Buendia in a false nine role and that experiment, albeit a forced one, panned out as expected as they registered just two touches in the opposition box before the red card and five in total.

They simply cannot approach the game against Arsenal without a focal point of the attack.

Seventeen-year-old Brian Madjo , who emerged in style with five goals in seven appearances throughout pre-season, is out injured and Watkins' usual understudy Tammy Abraham was also sidelined at Brighton.

Sky Sports News has reported the club are expected to act on their long-term interest in reuniting Nicolas Jackson and Emery, his old boss at Villarreal, if Watkins does depart - given the manner of their opening loss and the strength of their next opponent, urgency might be required.

The club have also made an approach to AC Milan for Rafael Leao , with the Portugal forward open to the move.

Villa have spent the least amount of any side in the league to replace the players they have lost this summer - and striker is not a position you can make do without.

Joao Gomes captured the hearts of Villa fans for his performances in pre-season, scoring in the 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich to cap off an impressive start to life in claret and blue.

However, like Villa as a whole, he unravelled against Brighton. Gomes was caught on the ball inside his own penalty area for Jack Hinshelwood's second, scored just 79 seconds after his first and Brighton's third, and the Brazilian was sent off for violent conduct soon after.

He will now serve a three-game suspension, giving Emery another headache.

His arrival was meant to ease the absence of Tielemans' departure but Emery will now have to rely on Ross Barkley, John McGinn, Lamare Bogarde or potentially Lindelof in midfield, as he did in the Europa League final.

Gomes was embraced by his manager as he trudged off the pitch after 40-minute Premier League debut to forget. A difficult afternoon for all involved but the problems have only worsened as a result of his red card.

A deal is currently being finalised to sign free agent Leon Goretzka and his experience, as well as leadership, is needed. Whether he could be thrust into the line-up against Arsenal remains to be seen.

Worrying insight into life without Konsa

The absence of a recognised striker at Brighton meant Villa's struggles going forward were to be expected. The defensive performance, on the other hand, was inexcusable.

Konsa's £55m move to Arsenal was arguably the most worrying of all the summer exits. The defending at the Amex offered a worrying insight into what life without the centre-back could be like.

Self-inflicted errors from Pau Torres, Lindelof failing to track runners in the box, and the lack of calmness that Villa would often rely on when Konsa was a pillar of the defence all contributed to the embarrassing display inside their own penalty box.

Brighton cut through their opponents with ease, so much so that they registered the highest expected goals tally from open play that Emery has faced since being appointed to the role in October 2022 (3.54 xG).

A bid has been rejected for Southampton centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis and contact has been made for Club Brugge defender Joel Ordanez but in the meantime, before the cavalry arrives, Villa have to cut out the individual errors.

Three of the 21 shots Brighton had came from Villa errors, of which two resulted in goals. If the same pattern unfolds at Villa Park, Arsenal will waste no time in replicating a similar onslaught.

The problems for Villa have piled up and while certain solutions are seemingly being worked on in the background, Emery and his threadbare squad may be forced to prove they can manage without them against the champions.

articles.standfirst: El francés no se entrenó en la sesión previa al partido contra la Real Sociedad y apunta a baja para el duelo
articles.summary: El francés no se entrenó en la sesión previa al partido contra la Real Sociedad
articles.body: Vuelve la incógnita sobre Tchouaméni. El francés no se ha ejercitado hoy junto a sus compañeros en la previa del partido ante la Real Sociedad, que será el debut del conjunto blanco en el Santiago Bernabéu esta temporada. Endrick, Militao, Mendy, Thiago, Rodrygo y Asencio siguen trabajando en sus respectivos procesos de recuperación y tampoco se les espera para el siguiente compromiso liguero.

articles.title: Transfer window 2026: What does your Premier League club need with a week to go?
articles.summary: BBC Sport takes a look at what each of the Premier League clubs still need before the summer transfer window shuts in seven days.
articles.body:
The first weekend of the Premier League season is complete but clubs still have one week of the transfer window remaining to secure last-minute squad additions.

Results are one thing but for many managers and sporting directors their opening match was an eye-opener in what positions need to be strengthened, who is no longer needed and what gaps still need to be plugged.

With the transfer window closing on Tuesday, 1 September at 23:00 BST, BBC Sport takes a look at what each top-flight club still needs and fans also have their say.

The Premier League champions have already strengthened the middle of the pitch with Bruno Guimaraes, the wing with Christos Tzolis and their defence with Ezri Konsa.

But Arsenal are still in the market for a forward and have a long-standing interest in Julian Alvarez.

Although it appears to be a difficult deal due to many factors, the Gunners will be ready to act if there is a chance to get it done.

If you want someone who is Premier League proven, who has won it all from the World Cup to the Champions League, Julian Alvarez looks like the guy that can take Arsenal to the promised land of finally getting over the line in Europe. Especially when there aren't that many elite forwards in the world.

Al-Hilal open talks to sign Arsenal winger Martinelli Published 1 day ago

What don't Aston Villa need after a raft of star departures this summer?

Ollie Watkins' transfer saga, with Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal trying to sign the striker, leaves Villa looking for a likely replacement with Nicolas Jackson a target.

A winger is also on the agenda while they need a defender after Ezri Konsa's move to Arsenal , and have opened talks for Club Brugge central defender Joel Ordonez after bids for Southampton centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis were rejected.

It is clear Aston Villa desperately require a striker more than anything right now.

Although I massively rate Victor Lindelof and Pau Torres, the display against Brighton has worried me slightly.

Therefore, I would welcome another centre-back as well.

It looks like we will be OK in midfield once Johan Manzambi is fit and with the addition of Leon Goretzka.

Watkins' departure would cut deepest - and Villa did not see it coming Published 1 day ago

Watkins' departure would cut deepest - and Villa did not see it coming

Villa in talks with Club Brugge for defender Ordonez Published 1 day ago

Villa in talks with Club Brugge for defender Ordonez

Bournemouth are used to being picked off and will simply be hoping to come through the final eight days of the transfer window unscathed.

It is clear that big clubs are circling for forward Eli Junior Kroupi and midfielder Alex Scott, who the Cherries insist are not for sale.

In terms of incomings, Bournemouth are largely done as they close in on a move for Juventus goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio.

Brentford are in the fortunate position of being able to choose their deals carefully after some excellent squad strengthening.

The Bees have been looking at left-back, with West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf strongly linked, but it hardly seems a matter of urgency with Keane Lewis-Potter able to play as a wing-back with Rico Henry and Aaron Hickey also in the mix.

There is experienced striking cover in the shape of former England international Callum Wilson and an all-round depth to Keith Andrews' squad that was missing last season.

Do not expect it to be a hectic closing few days in the transfer window.

Another forward option - particularly down the left - would take this window for Brentford from a nine to a 10 out of 10.

Mykhailo Mudryk's name has been doing the rounds in recent weeks and Brentford have history there, having chased him prior to his move to Chelsea .

Get someone like Mudryk in, and I don't think the transfer window could've gone much better for Andrews.

It is anticipated Yankuba Minteh will leave for Liverpool , which might create space at Brighton for another forward and Carlos Baleba's exit for Manchester United may see the club make a move for midfield reinforcements.

It is possible there may be other exits but, as usual, Brighton will stick to their data driven recruitment plan.

"We must continue to evolve, invest and innovate while remaining true to the principles that have brought us this far," was chairman Tony Bloom's message to fans before the 4-0 win against Aston Villa .

With Baleba's anticipated departure and Minteh looking likely that he might leave as well, we need to bring a defensive midfielder who can bring a physical presence to our midfield and a winger who is proven at the top level.

We have a lot of games this season with European football, so we need to have the squad depth to compete on all fronts if we want to secure a top-10 finish again.

Chelsea supporters may want another star forward or a new goalkeeper to replace the unconvincing Robert Sanchez, but Xabi Alonso feels his squad is largely complete for this summer.

However, there is a huge amount of work to do to reduce the squad from 39 players to around 25 within the next eight days. That is the priority, as the Blues will not want frustrated players in their squad this season.

Chelsea need to focus more on the outgoings than incoming players.

With no Europe it's important we do not carry a squad that's too heavy, as we won't have too much room for rotation.

If we were to bring anybody in, I think the priority is a top-drawer goalkeeper.

Coventry are in the hunt for Mykhailo Mudryk as the Chelsea winger looks to get his career back on track after serving a 20 month suspension for testing positive for banned substance meldonium.

Defensive cover is also likely to be needed by Frank Lampard while players like Luke Woolfenden could leave on loan.

Honestly, I think we have done enough in the transfer window to build a team that can stay up in this league.

There has been a lot of change at Palace with the loss of Maxence Lacroix and a new manager starting the season in Pierre Sage.

The Eagles have been building depth for their Europa League campaign but still need a few bodies in the building.

Sage has made clear he wants a senior centre-back and Palace could be pushed to sign another defender too after the injury to Chadi Riad in the first game of the Premier League season against Everton .

Riad's injury has amplified the need for another centre-back who is first-team ready.

Axel Disasi is a good start, but a bigger, permanent move would be great. That, plus a central midfielder, and we are set.

Mateta's contract claim leaves Palace with transfer decision Published 1 day ago

Mateta's contract claim leaves Palace with transfer decision

Everton simply must sign a recognised right-back before the window shuts. It has been a glaring problem for more than a year.

It is a weakness recognised by everyone at the club but either a prime target cannot be agreed upon or is out of reach.

Talented midfielder Merlin Rohl took on the job for the opening game against Crystal Palace, while Jake O'Brien and James Garner have also been pressed into service.

Time to finally make a decision and get one in. Maybe David Moyes will also look at adding another striker with questions still hanging over Beto and Thierno Barry.

Chelsea outcast Liam Delap is one name regularly linked with Everton .

Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has been clear that he is happy with the club's business so far, but more could be done to make his squad more balanced.

There have been attempts to sign an additional central defender, with a move for Rennes' Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal explored two weeks ago, and that could be a key area the Cottagers look to strengthen.

This is a club that does not operate at the very top end of the transfer market and one that enjoys a deadline-day deal.

It still feels like Fulham need a right winger - whether that is sticking with Oscar Bobb or providing serious competition for him - I think we need to cover for the loss of Harry Wilson's goals.

We also need a right-sided centre-back as there are serious concerns over how Joachim Anderson will fit Arbeloa's new system.

It has already been a busy summer for Hull City 's recruitment team but the ambitious Tigers are still working on adding two new forwards in Mohamed Ali-Cho and Ilyas Ansah.

There has also been interest from the club in Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia, although that deal has taken longer than hoped after the La Liga side raised their valuation of the 20-year-old. Stoke City's Sorba Thomas is also a player of interest.

A goalkeeper, midfielder and right-back also could be on the agenda for Sergej Jakirovic's side in the final week of the window.

Over the next week, if we bring in a left winger, one more striker - assuming the Ali-Cho deal also gets completed - a central midfielder, an attacking midfielder and a right-back to add depth and challenge Lewie Coyle for the starting spot, we will be in a strong position to compete.

Ipswich have spent over £150m on 12 new signings since returning to the Premier League.

Boss Gary O'Neil expects more, though, and a striker and a midfielder could arrive at Portman Road.

Fringe players like Anis Memeti could leave as O'Neil shapes his squad.

Having pushed the boat out to sign James Trafford from Manchester City , big money signings are probably off the agenda for Leeds in the last week of the window.

They are interested in taking Mykhailo Mudryk on loan but have not been able to strike a deal with the London club as yet as they are looking at other left wingers.

Leeds are also considering back-up options for forwards Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha and have also been linked with Frankfurt goalkeeper Michael Zetterer, if Lucas Perri joins Torino on loan as expected.

Leeds have had a great transfer window but they badly need another left-footed left-back as cover for Gabriel Gudmundsson.

Beyond that, perhaps another forward or creative midfielder to contend with Harry Wilson, Brenden Aaronson and Noah Okafor.

As has been the case for most of the summer, Liverpool 's priority remains the wide attacking areas and the expectation is that at least one and maybe two wingers will come in over the coming week.

Andoni Iraola said that personnel was not the issue when it came to defensive midfielders, the manner in which his side conceded twice at Newcastle would suggest that it would be wise to address Liverpool 's deficiencies in that department.

It is no secret Liverpool have been actively looking in the market for wingers - Bradley Barcola, Ibrahim Mbaye and Yankuba Minteh - and Sunday's display against Newcastle cemented that with Rio Ngumoha looking uncomfortable on the right.

However, the performance also showed Liverpool may need a defensive midfielder to plug the huge disconnect between the defence and midfield, especially on the counter attack.

Liverpool fans have been crying out for a Fabinho replacement since his departure, but it could be too late with a week to go.

Does Elliott have a Liverpool future after latest omission? Published 1 day ago

Does Elliott have a Liverpool future after latest omission?

Manchester City could well be one of the busiest sides to do business in the remaining days of the transfer window.

With Savinho gone and Omar Marmoush and Nico Gonzalez seemingly on their way out, there will be gaps in the squad which will need addressing.

A deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi has been agreed with Lille, and with Palmeiras for winger Allan, while BBC Sport has been told winger Pedro Neto remains of interest and speculation around signing Chelsea team-mate Enzo Fernandez continues.

Director of football Hugo Viana may have his hands full in these coming days.

City need numbers. We have let go of so many players, with Omar Marmoush and maybe Nico Gonzalez set to follow Rodri and Savinho out of the door alongside several others this summer.

It is essential that City bring in three or four new names before the deadline, with two of them being midfielders.

The maths whizz turned £86m teenage star heading to Man City Published 2 days ago

The maths whizz turned £86m teenage star heading to Man City

Man City agree deal for Palmeiras winger Allan Published 1 day ago

Man City agree deal for Palmeiras winger Allan

Carlos Baleba's arrival completes the midfield recruitment, now all eyes are on the left-back situation and whether Manchester United bring in someone to compete with Luke Shaw.

The club has a long-standing interest in Newcastle 's Lewis Hall, but are also assessing Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and have been heavily linked with Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander.

It is also possible they bring in another forward but that probably depends on one of their existing ones leaving, with Joshua Zirkzee the most likely.

A left-back is essential and this is not just a knee-jerk reaction to the defeat at Hull City - you can see United are short in that position.

We can not realistically expect Luke Shaw to play every game this season and there are still doubts as to whether Michael Carrick trusts Patrick Dorgu in defence.

Baleba completes £70m Man Utd move from Brighton Published 8 hours ago

Baleba completes £70m Man Utd move from Brighton

Man Utd's midfield spending is done - now for a left-back? Published 8 hours ago

Man Utd's midfield spending is done - now for a left-back?

Newcastle United 's young signings did not look fazed when they faced Liverpool on their Premier League debuts at the weekend.

Manager Matthias Jaissle could still use another midfielder with some top-flight nous, though, after Newcastle sold Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali, and the club are progressing with a move for Manchester City 's Nico Gonzalez.

Beyond that, bringing in a mobile and versatile forward who could chip in would help ease the burden on William Osula and Yoane Wissa.

Nottingham Forest are still working on deals after only bringing in three new faces so far this summer.

A striker and a full-back would be ideal with the club in talks for Chelsea 's Liam Delap, while Fiorentina right-back Dodo is of interest.

Boss Oliver Glasner has played down the need for midfield reinforcements, despite Elliot Anderson's departure to Manchester City .

Forest working on deal for Chelsea striker Delap Published 1 day ago

Forest working on deal for Chelsea striker Delap

With the signings of French full-back Dayann Methalie from Toulouse and Antwerp midfielder Jules Ahoka over the line, the obvious position Sunderland still need to fill is right wing.

Sporting's Geny Catamo is the name most heavily linked.

Asked about reported interest from the Premier League, Sporting boss Rui Borges insisted Catamo is "happy" at the Portuguese club, but we have seen before that does not necessarily mean much.

Given Eliezer Mayenda has left, meaning Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor are the club's only first-team strikers, another forward who plays through the middle is probably needed.

Spurs have strengthened by spending heavily in the summer, but if Dominic Solanke is not going to be used regularly as a main striker, then this is where Roberto de Zerbi must look next.

Richarlison took the starting role in the opening weekend loss at Brentford , and while a deal for Manchester City's Omar Marmoush is progressing , is this actually his best role?

Tottenham desperately need forward players who can turn De Zerbi's quick attacks into decisive moments.

Currently Spurs have the players to play through pressure but don't have the players to maximise the situations this creates.

A winger and a striker who can improve us will be a drastic upgrade.

articles.title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools
articles.summary: Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences
articles.body:
Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct.

York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement, according to prosecutors.

York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.

Records also show that York had his cell phone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.

Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.

"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email.

"You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offences in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."

The 49ers Enterprises - who are the investment arm of York's San Francisco 49ers - own Leeds United. The Premier League club have declined to comment.

They are also part of the US consortium who acquired a majority shareholding in Rangers last summer. However, York is not listed on the club's list of board members.

When contacted by Sky Sports News, Rangers chose not to comment.

A San Francisco 49ers statement read: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."

The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy.

Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy.

articles.title: How did record nine new managers fare in opening round of Premier League games?
articles.summary: Who impressed and who has work to do? BBC Sport chief football writer Phil McNulty looks at how the nine new managerial appointments fared on the opening week of the Premier League season.
articles.body:
Premier League history was made before a ball was even kicked this season as a record nine clubs started the season with new managers.

The post-Pep Guardiola era has begun at Manchester City under Enzo Maresca, while Andoni Iraola got his first taste of action as Liverpool manager after succeeding sacked Arne Slot. Xabi Alonso is the latest with his foot in the revolving door of managers at Chelsea .

So how did the new faces fare after an eventful first weekend of the new campaign?

The German successor to Iraola came within six minutes of starting his Premier League career with a statement win at Manchester City , only to concede two late goals to suffer a heartbreaking loss.

He will be frustrated at the manner of City's goals, with Marc Guehi unmarked at a corner for the equaliser then a slow reaction for Josko Gvardiol's stoppage time winner, but Rose was also shown in those first 84 minutes that he has plenty of materials to work with in a Cherries side that finished sixth last season.

Rose will have seen enough to deliver early signs of encouragement amid the disappointment of such a painful late loss.

Not a bad start to take the lead after 31 seconds and a satisfactory start to Alonso's reign, but there was obvious good and obvious bad in what he watched at Craven Cottage.

The attacking triumvirate of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and newcomer Morgan Rogers hit the ground running, all scoring and combining to devastating effect.

Equally devastating to Chelsea 's Premier League chances and the Alonso revival could be the failure to find a better goalkeeper than the unreliable Robert Sanchez, who was at fault for both Fulham goals.

Alonso must find an answer quickly otherwise what Palmer, Joao Pedro and Rogers give with one hand Sanchez could take away with both hands.

Tactically Alonso used a back three with Reece James operating in midfield but also dropping back into defence.

Disappointing start for the highly-regarded Sage, who did such an outstanding job at Lens, with defeat at Everton but he also knows the outcome could have been a much more satisfactory one.

Palace's second half display will have disappointed him, but they had chances in the opening period to set up their first win at Everton since 2014. They hit the woodwork twice, while Jean-Phillipe Mateta was wasteful. Sage and his team paid a heavy price.

Sage's unhappy opening weekend will not have been helped by a contract row surrounding striker Mateta that puts his future in question, while he will want more numbers and quality to add to his squad.

Next up Manchester City at Selhurst Park, where Sage will sample the superb night game atmosphere as he searches for his first league win. No easy task.

Tough opener and conceding within the first minute did not help Arbeloa's cause as he builds after taking over from Marco Silva.

It is already clear he needs to make sure Fulham can find some goals, although he will be delighted young debutant Gonzalo Garcia got off the mark. It was more of a struggle for another new arrival from Real Madrid, Cesar Palacios.

The jewel in Arbeloa's crown will be 19-year-old Josh King, who he described as "unbelievable". It is already clear the youngster will bear a heavy weight of responsibility under Fulham 's new management.

Ipswich Town have backed Kieran McKenna's successor with big money in the transfer market, £150m on a dozen signings, and Gary O'Neil was rewarded with a vital victory against Sunderland .

O'Neil may just be the beneficiary from lessons learned during Ipswich's last spell in the Premier League, when they took 11 games to get a win and went down with a whimper with just 22 points.

He will have been delighted with the impact of Julio Enciso, who he worked with at Strasbourg, and his early partnership with Brazilian striker Emersonn, the pair combining superbly for the latter's opening goal.

Plenty still to work on but O'Neil looked in the mood to enjoy his cup of tea and bar of chocolate while watching Match Of The Day on Saturday night.

Iraola was spared the ignominy of defeat in his first Premier League game since succeeding Arne Slot by Dominik Szoboszlai's 99th minute penalty – but this was a sobering fact-finding mission for the new man in charge at Anfield.

He did not seem unduly concerned, but both Newcastle United 's goals will have been hauntingly familiar to those who watched Liverpool 's title defence collapse under Slot last season.

Newcastle cashed in on Liverpool 's wide open midfield, a flaw from the last campaign that saw them so vulnerable to fast counter-attacks. Anthony Elanga sliced through Liverpool for the first then six of Iraola's team stood idly by as Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock combined for the second.

Iraola has suggested Liverpool will not strengthen in midfield with a 'number 6' type defensively-minded player. This early evidence (not to mention what was seen last season) suggests he should.

If not, the draw at Newcastle was a red flag showing Iraola needs to find an internal solution which is not currently obvious.

It's all very well targeting wide players such as Bradley Barcola and Yankuba Minteh, but what about when teams are running straight through the heart of Liverpool 's team?

Iraola must also find a way to make the subdued Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz look like the players Liverpool paid £241m for. Both were poor again at St. James' Park.

It looked like it was going to be a losing start for Guardiola's successor before Manchester City pulled it around with two late goals to beat Bournemouth .

How Maresca needed it after City were pounded by Arsenal in the Community Shield. The Italian's emotions at the final whistle looked as much relief as celebration. He needs wins just to settle post-Guardiola nerves and ease the transition.

Maresca described the day as "perfect". It very nearly wasn't.

Erling Haaland's crop is not the only new look at City this season, but on occasions there were passages of play with lots of possession but little punch, a familiar pattern from Maresca's time at Leicester City and Chelsea . The use of Marc Guehi in midfield was a tactical twist.

Maresca will have wanted the win, no matter how it came, and City achieved it, even though it did carry a lot of the hallmarks of a work in progress.

Seconds away from what would have been a very significant win against Liverpool , but still plenty for Jaissle to take away even with the concession of that late, late penalty.

The Toon Army were right behind the new manager and his team, reshaping after the loss of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, and they responded with real intensity.

The effort was there, the attacking style Jaissle wants was there, only the win was missing but enough to please him after fall-out from this summer's Tyneside turbulence.

Poor start for the Austrian who brought FA Cup and Europa League success to Crystal Palace , losing 1-0 to a late Leeds United goal at The City Ground.

Glasner claimed he cannot simply lay hands on players and they perform like "Real Madrid in the 70s", but this still was an unsatisfactory opening as he tries to bring stability and success to Nottingham Forest and their demanding owner Evangelos Marinkis after four managers were in charge last season.

He had no new signings in his starting line-up, with eight from Nuno Espirito Santo's team in the opening-day win over Brentford last season, although it looks like striker Liam Delap might arrive from Chelsea .

Every Forest manager needs wins (and very quickly) so to make a losing introduction was a real blow for Glasner.

articles.title: Carabao Cup 2026-27: How does prize money work in the competition?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains how prize money works in the EFL Cup
articles.body:
Compared to other cup competitions such as the FA Cup and Champions League, the EFL Cup uses a different payment structure when it comes to prize money for teams.

While most competitions have a structured round-by-round monetary prize, including in its qualifying rounds, the EFL Cup only has specific round prize money from the semi-finals onward.

The EFL Cup winners get £100,000 in prize money. For comparison, this season's FA Cup winners will earn just over £2.1m in prize money.

Instead of a large prize pot, clubs earn revenue in a number of different ways, with the English Football League seeing those as effectively the competition's prize money.

In the EFL Cup, clubs are offered an equal split of gate receipts regardless of the two teams in the fixture. This can benefit lower league clubs if they are drawn away to a big Premier League side that has a larger stadium than they do.

Should a club sell 40,000 tickets for a match at £20 each, it would equate to £800,000 in gate receipts.

Clubs can also achieve significant earnings through EFL Cup Facility Fees. This means that clubs can pocket a fee starting from £75,000 if their match is shown on Sky Sports' main channel, increasing depending on how far they progress in the competition.

The EFL Cup is worth around £110m a season to the EFL, including around £70m going to EFL clubs in central payments with additional monies to Premier League and EFL clubs from direct earnings.

articles.title: El verano de Aday Mara: a días de su estreno con la selección absoluta y mimado por los Thunder
articles.standfirst: El pívot debutará este viernes en las Ventanas FIBA tras haber trabajado con la nueva directora de rendimiento atlético enviada desde Oklahoma
articles.summary: El pívot debutará este viernes en las Ventanas FIBA tras haber trabajado con la nueva directora de rendimiento atlético enviada desde Oklahoma
articles.body: La selección española llegó este lunes a Zaragoza, donde este viernes se mide a Portugal en el estreno de la segunda fase de las Ventanas FIBA de clasificación para la Copa del Mundo que se celebrará en Qatar el próximo año. La cabeza visible del equipo fue Aday Mara y no sólo por sus largos 2,21 metros. También porque el joven pívot hará su debut con la absoluta y será en Zaragoza, donde nació y debutó en la Liga Endesa. Mara ya ha posado con la camiseta roja en la sesión oficial de fotos previa a los partidos y se ha entrenado sobre el parqué del Príncipe Felipe. España se medirá también a Grecia este lunes 31 de agosto. El pívot ha formado parte de algunos combinados de formación y ha subido a podios (platas en el Mundial U17 de 2022 y en el Eurobasket U18 de 2023), pero ahora se encuentra a horas de su primer partido con la absoluta. "Muy feliz de debutar con la selección y luego de poderlo hacer aquí en casa, con amigos, familia y gente que conozco entre el público. Desde que salió que iba a venir a jugar aquí llevo pensándolo, pero intento alejarme lo más posible para que no influya en el partido en entrenos", asegura el pívot en sus primeras palabras desde Zaragoza. El regreso a casa le ha hecho acordarse de sus inicios: "Esos momentos en los que, empezando desde infantiles a alevines, venías a entrenar a la pista de goma y luego tenías que pasar a la de parqué y luego pasabas a la central... Recordar todo eso y el proceso y todas las relaciones que ibas haciendo es algo súper bonito". El pívot de 21 años vive un verano trascendental en su todavía corta carrera en la que ya se proclamó campeón de la NCAA con una Universidad de Míchigan la temporada pasada. Además de su estreno con la absoluta le espera la NBA después de haber sido elegido por los Thunder en el último draft en la duodécima posición. Preparando ese otro debut ha estado trabajando durante varias semanas. Para ayudarle en el proceso de adaptación a la Liga estadounidenses, la franquicia de Oklahoma, campeona en 2025, envió a España a Maral Javadifar, su nueva directora de rendimiento atlético. Se trata de una muestra de la fe y el interés que tienen los Thunder en que Mara pueda desarrollar todo su potencial cuanto antes en la NBA. Lo importante es que mejore su físico y se adapte al vertiginoso ritmo de la competición. Javadifar, que trabajó con el prodigio español durante su estancia en Tenerife, es una profesional muy bien considerada en su ámbito. Durante siete años formó parte de los Tampa Bay Buccaneers de la NFL, campeones de la Super Bowl en 2021. En junio de este año se incorporó a los Thunder y una de sus primeras misiones es dirigir el desarrollo físico de un portento como el de Mara, que ya ha participado en encuentros con su nuevo equipo en la Liga de Verano de la NBA. La primera oportunidad que tendrá el pívot español de mostrar sus evoluciones será este viernes frente a Portugal y en Zaragoza, su casa. Puede ser el inicio de una nueva era en la selección.

articles.title: Sancris vuelve a casa para reforzar el ataque del Lega... desde Getafe
articles.standfirst: El atacante llega cedido por el club azulón con una opción de compra condicionada
articles.summary: El atacante llega cedido por el Getafe con una opción de compra condicionada
articles.body: Álex Sancris ya es nuevo jugador del Leganés. El conjunto pepinero ha alcanzado un acuerdo con el Getafe para la cesión por una temporada del atacante madrileño, de 29 años. La operación incluye además una opción de compra condicionada al término del curso. Su llegada supone el regreso a una casa que conoce perfectamente. Sancris militó durante cuatro temporadas en el filial pepinero, al que llegó en 2018 procedente del Trival Valderas. Fue capitán, logró el ascenso a Segunda Federación y en su última campaña firmó 10 goles antes de abandonar el club en 2022. Después pasó por el Linares y dio el salto al fútbol profesional con el Burgos, donde sus dos buenas temporadas le abrieron las puertas del Getafe. Ahora regresa a Butarque para ponerse a las órdenes de Rubén Albés y reforzar un ataque en el que ya están Unax del Cura, Gothler y Álex Millán. El fichaje tiene también un componente personal. Sancris volverá a compartir vestuario con Miguel Atienza, con quien mantiene una buena amistad después de coincidir durante su etapa en el Burgos. Sancris se marcha así al club en el que también jugó en categorías inferiores, al igual que pasó en Getafe. Tras una temporada con pocos minutos, Bordalás dejó claro que no contaba con el futbolista, que este curso no ha disputado minutos ni siquiera en pretemporada, donde no ha estado ni siquiera convocado. Pese a ello, en el Getafe siguen pensando que Sancris es un jugador que puede aportar en un futuro, por lo que el conjunto pepinero sólo tendrá esa opción de compra en caso de ascenso. Con ello, el Getafe sigue acelerando la operación salida a falta aún de que se ejecute en otros jugadores como Berrocal, Javi Muñoz y Neyou.

articles.title: Goodbye Savinho, hello Savio: Tottenham sign winger from Man City for £75m
articles.summary: Tottenham sign Brazil winger Savinho from Manchester City for an initial £75m - and he reverts to being called Savio.
articles.body:
"Wishing you all the best, Savinho", wrote Manchester City on social media platform X , external .

"Welcome to Tottenham , Savio", announced Spurs. , external

The 22-year-old Brazil winger has joined the Londoners for an initial fee of £75m - and a new start has come with a new name.

In 2024 he said his national team put Savinho on his shirt, and he asked City to keep it for luck when he moved there in 2024.

But now the attacker, whose full name is Savio Moreira de Oliveira, has reverted back and will be known as Savio on his number 17 shirt, not Savinho.

He has signed a long-term contract, with Roberto de Zerbi's side potentially paying a further £10m in add-ons.

'Energy, imagination and quality' - a move a year in the making

Savio's move to north London has been more than 12 months in the making, with Spurs failing in a bid to sign him last summer when Thomas Frank was in charge.

He opted to remain at Etihad Stadium, but his game time was limited under former City boss Pep Guardiola last term, making just seven Premier League starts.

"It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here," said Savio, who has 13 caps for his country but was not part of their World Cup squad.

"It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world.

"As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team."

Savio joined City from French side Troyes in a £30.8m deal two years ago and made 84 appearances, scoring seven goals and providing 16 assists.

His arrival at Spurs follows those of Mateus Fernandes from West Ham, Sandro Tonali from Newcastle and Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton this summer, with spending reaching a combined £312m.

Spurs have also brought in defenders Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson, and goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, on free transfers.

"Savio is a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity," added De Zerbi.

Spurs are also in advanced talks to buy Egypt forward Omar Marmoush from City, and sources with knowledge of the situation say there is a "good chance" the deal gets completed before the 1 September transfer deadline.

Savio's involvement for City fell sharply last season after the club signed winger Antoine Semenyo from Bournemouth in January.

He played 821 Premier League minutes, scoring once and providing one assist, while featuring in only 31% of City's available minutes across all competitions.

That was a significant drop from the previous campaign, when he played 54% of City's minutes.

Yet his 2024-25 numbers show why Tottenham are prepared to invest heavily in him. Savio registered eight Premier League assists that season, all from open play, despite playing only 1,773 minutes. Only five players recorded more from open play.

On a per-90 basis, he ranked third for open-play assists with 0.41, while only Mohamed Salah created more chances per 90 than Savio's 2.2.

His biggest threat, though, came from carrying the ball. Among Premier League players with at least 1,000 minutes in 2024-25, only Jeremy Doku averaged more progressive carries of at least 10 metres than Savio's 6.8 per 90 minutes.

Savio also led the division for carries followed by a chance created, averaging 1.3 per 90, while only Son Heung-min ended a carry with an assist more frequently. Savio also completed 2.6 dribbles per 90 with a 51% success rate and used those carries to draw defenders towards him before releasing team-mates.

That ability was even more evident during his breakout 2023-24 season on loan at Girona. Savio played 2,989 minutes in La Liga in 2023-24, with 65% of them coming on the left wing. He scored nine goals, supplied eight assists and established himself as one of the division's most dangerous one-against-one players.

At City his role shifted. Across his two Premier League seasons, his most common position was on the right, accounting for 36% of his minutes, compared with 20% on the left. That versatility could matter at Spurs.

articles.title: Julián Alvarez y los otros futbolistas que forzaron para jugar en el Barça
articles.standfirst: El argentino es el último ejemplo de una lista de jugadores que llevaron al límite a sus clubes para poder fichar por el conjunto azulgrana
articles.summary: El argentino es el último ejemplo de una lista de jugadores que llevaron al límite a sus clubes para poder fichar por el conjunto azulgrana
articles.body: A falta de una semana para el cierre de mercado la situación de Julián Alvarez parece más estancada que nunca. El Arsenal parece querer en el horizonte, pero el deseo del jugador, su sueño, sigue siendo jugar en el Barcelona. El argentino es el último de una lista de jugadores que forzaron para cumplir dicho sueño. Teniendo contrato en vigor siempre complica mucho salir de un club, más aún cuando el destino es un rival directo por los títulos. Es el caso de Julián, que tiene el sueño de vestir de azulgrana, pero el Atlético se niega en rotundo. Las palabras del jugador durante el Mundial forzaron la máquina y su actitud en su estreno liguero volvió a reflejar su malestar con el club colchonero.  Dos pruebas claras de su forma de presionar para que le dejen salir. Pero esto no es nuevo y por eso repasamos algunos de los ejemplos más sonados de jugadores que presionaron al máximo para fichar por el Barça. A finales de los 90 el Barça era muy partidario de fichar jugadores neerlandeses. Los hermanos de Boer, especialmente Frank, interesaban mucho y los dos presionaron al máximo al Ajax para fichar por el Barça. El club de Amsterdam no cedía y los jugadores fueron hasta la comisión de arbitraje de la federación de su país para romper su contrato y poder, por fin, vestir de azulgranas. El camerunés tenía que lidiar con el Real Madrid y con el Mallorca, dueños de sus derechos. Con los baleares hubo acuerdo rápido, pero con los madridistas no. Florentino Pérez se resistió a dejarle ir y Eto'o publicó incluso un comunicado en la prensa dirigido a los culés para mostrar su deseo de jugar para ellos. Finalmente, los blancos cedieron y el delantero vistió de azulgrana tras pagar 27 millones de euros. Un futbolista criado en La Masía que decidió probar suerte muy joven en el Arsenal. Allí, en Londres, terminó triunfando y cuando le quiso el Barça no lo dudó. Pero los 'gunners' no lo pusieron nada fácil. No faltó a los entrenamientos, pero los hacía en solitario. Finalmente pudo vestir de nuevo de azulgrana en 2011 previo pago de 35 millones de euros. El argentino es el perfecto ejemplo de jugador que hace lo que sea por cumplir su sueño. Incluso pagar. Corría el año 2010 y el Liverpool no le dejaba salir y, si lo hacía, el Inter de Milán era el deseado. Pero el centrocampista sólo quería el Barça y tuvo que pagar tres de los 24 millones de euros que le costó al cuadro azulgrana para poder vestir sus colores. "Luché por estar acá y acá estoy", dijo en su presentación. El extremo francés soñaba en azul y grana. Y lo cumplió, pero también le costó lo suyo. El Borussia Dortmund, donde empezó a despuntar, no quería venderlo, pero el Barça lo quería ya. El jugador apretó tanto que incluso se encontraba en paradero desconocido como diría más tarde su entrenador Peter Bosz. Al final, el jugador se salió con la suya y fue al Barça, que tuvo que desembolsar 148 millones de euros. El brasileño fue uno de los traspasos más complicados. El Liverpool no quería traspasar a su estrella, que cuando supo del interés del Barça no quiso otra cosa más que ir a la Ciudad Condal. Forzó tanto que incluso presentó un 'transfer request' para que lo liberaran, pero no lo consiguió. Eso fue en verano, porque en invierno sí pudo realizar su sueño. El Barça tiró la casa por la ventana en el mercado invernal y lo tuvo pagando 135 millones de euros. Como pasa con Julián, el Atlético se negaba a dejarle salir. Hubo una primera vez que estuvo a punto, pero el jugador decidió seguir de rojiblanco con una decisión mediática tomada en un documental. Pero, al siguiente, el francés sí vio bien su cambio. En 2019 no se presentó a los entrenamientos y, tras pagar su cláusula de 120 millones de euros, se unió al Barça. El polaco es uno de los últimos ejemplos de la historia reciente. El Bayern Munich se negaba a dejarlo salir. Sabía que perdería una importante cantidad de goles, pero Lewy aseguró que su etapa en Alemania había terminado y que sólo quería ir al Barça. Pudo cumplir su sueño en 2022 previo pago de 45 millones de euros.

articles.title: El Barcelona ya ha encontrado a su '9'
articles.standfirst: Sportium sitúa a Raphinha como el gran rival de Mbappé en la lucha por el 'Pichichi' de LaLiga
articles.summary: Sportium sitúa a Raphinha como el gran rival de Mbappé en la lucha por el 'Pichichi' de LaLiga
articles.body: El Barcelona lleva todo el verano peleando por el fichaje de Julián Álvarez... pero todo parece indicar que el delantero argentino se quedará en el Atlético de Madrid. El club azulgrana trabaja en algún movimiento de última hora para incorporar otro ariete que ayude a cubrir las salidas de Lewandowski y Ferran. Flick, sin embargo, parece haber encontrado en Raphinha a su nuevo '9' en caso de emergencia. Una decisión que está teniendo impacto en las apuestas deportivas. Flick, desde luego, le ha cambiado la vida a Raphinha en el Barcelona. Cuando llegó el técnico alemán, el brasileño tenía colgado el cartel de transferible... pero terminó convirtiéndose en el jugador que mejor representa su estilo. Marcó 34 goles en su primera temporada a sus órdenes y la pasada, aun teniendo bastantes lesiones, llegó hasta los 21. Sin duda, los mejores años de su carrera. Acostumbrado a partir como extremo por la banda izquierda, Flick lo ubicó como delantero en el estreno liguero contra el Elche. La prueba salió a pedir de boca: Raphinha marcó dos goles y repartió una asistencia, convirtiéndose en uno de los grandes protagonistas de la goleada azulgrana. Todo apunta a que tendrá continuidad en esta nueva posición y Sportium ya ha tomado nota. De hecho, sitúa a Raphinha como el gran rival de Mbappé en la lucha por el 'Pichichi' de LaLiga. El brasileño cuenta con una cuota de 9.0 para terminar la temporada como máximo goleador, todavía bastante por detrás del delantero del Real Madrid, pero ya por delante de buena parte de los grandes candidatos al premio. Las mejores casas de apuestas así comienzan a reflejar el impacto que puede tener el cambio de posición del brasileño durante toda la temporada. Al Barcelona le toca recibir esta semana al Athletic Club en el Camp Nou, una prueba de mayor exigencia para comprobar si Raphinha mantiene su nueva posición de referencia ofensiva. El brasileño, además, tiene buenos antecedentes ante el conjunto dirigido por Edin Terzic, al que ha marcado tres goles en los ocho partidos que ha disputado frente a ellos. Sportium paga a 2.15 que vuelva a ver portería en este próximo encuentro.

articles.title: Chelsea Women: Sonia Bompastor and Ellie Carpenter on Blues' transitional moment as they target WSL and Champions League success
articles.summary: Chelsea are morphing into a new team under Sonia Bompastor; they are taking learning from a disappointing 2025/26 season, with a clear change in playing personnel; they want to return to WSL and domestic glory, as well as competing in the Champions League
articles.body:
Not pundit analysis, but the thoughts of Chelsea head coach Sonia Bompastor to Sky Sports ahead of the new WSL season.

And despite the hint of cliché, it works. There has been plenty upheaval over the last two years, starting with Bompastor replacing Emma Hayes.

Then, there was the shock departure of Paul Green as head of women's football in February. Alongside Hayes, the duo oversaw years of unprecedented success. It is something hard to sustain and even harder to replicate.

But that is the task that falls at Bompastor's feet. She managed to keep it going in her first season with an unbeaten domestic treble - some may say with Hayes' influence still in play - but her second campaign exposed the realties. Chelsea were not the team of old and a new era was beckoning.

Now in her third pre-season with the Blues, Bompastor believes she has the backing of the club to do just that.

"I think now I understand what the club is about a lot more," she said. "I also understand what we want to achieve and bringing my input into that.

"It's good to be in a place where I feel the confidence and the trust coming from the hierarchy in the club. As much as I know my job, we need to get good results in order for me to stay as long as possible, but it's also important to feel like we also have time to rebuild the team in order for us to compete against the best."

Chelsea only won the League Cup last season and finished third in the league behind Manchester City and Arsenal. It was the first time in six years they had not walked away with the WSL title.

Bompastor reflected: "We wanted last season to be a more successful season because Chelsea is a club who is used to winning. We only won one trophy, but if you analyse it, we have some good learnings to take and that's really important for us to reflect on.

"We spoke a lot about the environment and the culture we want to create here at Chelsea.

"It's a lot about standards, behaviours, how you show up every day, how much you are committing to work hard to achieve your goals and what are the type of behaviours you want to show up every day, off and on pitch.

"Who do we want to be as a team? How do we want people to talk about Chelsea? These things are really important for us to be able to achieve the goals we have.

"Chelsea are a club who are used to winning and we need to make sure we put everything together in order for us to achieve that.

"I'm quite happy with the squad of players I have, the quality we have, but it's also important alongside that quality to bring the right mentality."

Experience and youth informing transfer policy

This summer does have the air of a new start about it, especially in terms of playing personnel.

Players who have been the face of Chelsea for years have left. Former captain Millie Bright retired, legendary goalscorer Sam Kerr moved to the USA. Niamh Charles, Guro Reiten and Johanna Rytting Kaneryd also departed. They represent years of service, experience and trophies.

"We lost some really important players in terms of the environment and culture," Bompastor said. "Some of them had been here for many years and it's difficult to replace them.

"So it's for us, the staff and club, to think about how and what is the best way to replace them. It's about the recruitment, but also again linked back to the environment and the culture we want to create.

"We have also great leaders who have the right mentality about when you are on pitch, it's about winning games. Off the pitch, it's about the behaviours you need and showing up every day in order for us to work hard on the pitch to achieve the goals."

Chelsea's transfer strategy of mixing experience and youth is clear and epitomised by two of their four summer signings so far in Katie McCabe and Nelly Las.

McCabe needs little introduction. Indeed, Bompastor herself told Sky Sports she did not need to speak on the defender's quality, and it is clear she goes a long way in replacing some of the leadership Chelsea lost.

"She has already started to impact the squad in terms of the behaviours and the standards," Bompastor added. "I'm really pleased she's a Chelsea player now."

Las, meanwhile, is an exciting 18-year-old prospect who joined from Leicester. She made 16 WSL appearances across the last two seasons, and has featured for England's youth teams.

"It's important to have the right balance between experienced players, but also the youth into the squad," Bompastor said. "Players having versatility to play in different positions is also really important for me.

"I'm a manager who really loves to work with young players, to invest time to develop them and I'm really keen to bring these players into the squad and see how they can develop to contribute to the success we will have in the future."

There will always be pressure to win at Chelsea given their history, and they now have a balance to strike - maintaining that legacy while also forging a new way forward and meeting the standards Bompastor has set out.

That falls, in part, to the team's senior players - no matter how long they have played for the club.

One of those is defender Ellie Carpenter. She may have only been at Chelsea for a year, but as a multiple-trophy winner and regular starter, she will likely now step into a leadership role among the group.

"Chelsea are going through a bit of a transition phase at the moment. A lot of legends have gone and they left such a great legacy," she told Sky Sports. "Now it's our turn to do that, follow in their footsteps and to build on what Chelsea is as a club.

"As a footballer, you love those opportunities and moments in your career and it's a perfect time to be stepping into that role for this club.

"Our aim this season is to fight for those trophies back and show what Chelsea is about. We want to do it as a team, winning in that way and enjoying it and hopefully getting the results on the way as well.

"We have a great team this season and pre-season has felt good so I'm excited."

One way this squad can cement themselves into Chelsea history is by winning the one trophy that continues to elude them - the Champions League.

For a long time, the Blues' recruitment strategy has been geared towards European glory while the domestic trophies took care of themselves.

Bompastor won it as a manager with Lyon and was a key reason for her appointment in 2024. Carpenter was in her victorious squad, as was new striker Melvine Malard and defender Kadeisha Buchanan. McCabe won it with Arsenal. Lucy Bronze - who signed a new Chelsea deal this summer - has been crowned Europe champion five times.

But none of those have come in Chelsea blue and every year, we ask the same question: is this the year the wait is over?

"Winning the Champions League is one of the main goals for us," Bompastor said. "We'll work as hard as possible to achieve that and I know everyone is expecting Chelsea to always be at their best.

"But the competition now in Europe is getting higher and higher. Many clubs now are in a position where they can compete to win the Champions League. I don't want to shy away from us and our ambitions, but I also know it's difficult.

"But that's the one trophy we're missing in the club and we will try as hard as possible to fight for that."

"It's always what Chelsea want," Carpenter added. "It's what their ambition is, what the fans want, what everyone here wants and what we work towards every day.

"This squad is young, but multiple people have won it in the team, so that helps a lot to bring the experience and what it takes to win.

"But we're just going to go game-by-game this season. We don't want to put too much pressure on ourselves. When we're enjoying football, we're playing our best football."

While it may seem a tedious back and forth on the Champions League each year, that is the kind of scrutiny that comes with being at Chelsea and despite changes elsewhere, will never alter.

It has perhaps been one of the learnings for Bompastor in her two years at the club, and something she must instil in the squad she is assembling.

"I've never been in a place before where the scrutiny is so high like at Chelsea, but I'm comfortable with it," she reflected.

"It means people care about us and really think we are a really important club. That's what comes with our standards and Chelsea being one of the best clubs in the world, so we need to get comfortable with that.

"We need to make sure when we go into the season, we don't have any regrets and we give our all any time we step into the pitch."

What is for sure is the Blues are in the process of morphing into something new. Consistent evolution was one of the secrets to Hayes' success, and Bompastor will be hoping the same is true now.

articles.title: PFA Awards: Sir Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney win merit awards
articles.summary: Liverpool and Scotland legend Sir Kenny Dalglish and Lionesses great Karen Carney win the Professional Footballers' Association's merit awards for 2026.
articles.body:
Sir Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney have won the Professional Footballers' Association's merit awards for 2026.

The awards honour individuals who have made a lasting contribution to football.

The PFA Awards ceremony will be held in Manchester on Tuesday evening, where the men's and women's players' player of the year winners will be announced.

Dalglish enjoyed a prolific career as both player and manager, becoming Scotland's most-capped men's international with 102 appearances and matching Denis Law's national team record of 30 goals.

At club level, he began with a trophy-laden spell at Celtic before moving to Liverpool for a British record fee in 1977 and becoming an integral part of the club's golden era.

Over the next 14 years, Dalglish won eight First Division titles and three European Cups across 515 appearances for Liverpool and was runner-up for the Ballon d'Or in 1983.

Appointed player-manager in 1985, he guided the club to three league titles and two FA Cups - including the Double in 1985-86 - before retiring from playing in 1990.

After resigning as Liverpool's manager in February 1991, Dalglish led Blackburn to the Premier League title in 1995 and had stints with Celtic, Newcastle and Liverpool again, where he won the 2012 League Cup.

Off the field, Dalglish remains a significant figure in Merseyside. He led the club through the aftermath of the Hillsborough disaster in 1989, earning praise for his support of the bereaved families, and has raised millions of pounds to support cancer care and treatment through the Marina Dalglish Appeal, set up in 2005 following his wife's treatment for breast cancer.

Dalglish, 75, announced in June 2026 that he is having treatment for cancer.

Former England attacking midfielder Carney was a member of the Arsenal side that completed a historic quadruple in 2006-07 - winning the league, FA Cup, League Cup and Uefa Women's Cup, the forerunner to the Women's Champions League.

She spent two seasons with Chicago Red Stars before returning in 2011 to home club Birmingham City, where she had started her career. Carney scored an extra-time equaliser as Birmingham won the FA Cup the following season.

Moving to Chelsea in late 2015, Carney won the WSL and FA Cup double in 2017-18 and later served as club captain before ending her playing career in 2019.

On the international stage, Carney made her England debut as a 17-year-old in 2005. She went on to score 32 goals in 144 appearances for the Lionesses and helped England finish third at the 2015 Women's World Cup.

That was one of eight major tournaments for Carney with England, while she also represented Great Britain at the 2012 Olympics.

Since retiring, Carney, 39, has built a career as a broadcaster and analyst and was appointed by the UK Government to chair an independent review, published in 2023, into the future of domestic women's football.

articles.title: Oficial: Savinho, nuevo jugador del Tottenham
articles.standfirst: El club de Londres pagará al Manchester City 87 millones de euros más 13 en variables
articles.summary: El club de Londres pagará al Manchester City 87 millones de euros más 13 en variables
articles.body: El Tottenham Hotspur ha llegado a un acuerdo con el Manchester City para el traspaso del internacional brasileño Savinho por 75 millones de libras (87 millones de euros) más 10 en variables (13 millones). Los 'Spurs' se han gastado 330 millones en este mercado de fichajes, a la espera de la llegada del egipcio Omar Marmoush, también del City, por el que pagarán alrededor de 70 millones. El Tottenham ha incorporado este verano a Matheus Fernandes, Sandro Tonali y Jan Paul Van Hecke, en un intento de mejorar las prestaciones de las dos últimas temporadas y volver a competir en Europa. Savinho, de 22 años, llega al Tottenham tras dos años poco fructíferos en el City en los que ha disputado 53 partidos, marcado dos goles y repartido once asistencias. El brasileño, que previamente estuvo cedido en el Girona, ya estuvo cerca de irse al Tottenham el pasado verano, pero los 'Sky Blues' no aceptaron la oferta de 60 millones que recibió. En dos años, el valor de Savinho se ha duplicado. De los 40 millones que pagaron al Troyes, equipo que también pertenece al City Group y en el que Savinho no jugó ni un partido, a los 87 que han ingresado por él este verano y pese a que su rol en el equipo ha sido residual. La venta de Savinho es la más grande en la historia del City, superando por lo que vendieron a Julián Álvarez al Atlético en 2024, estimado en 75 millones de euros más 20 en variables.
